title: Linear Inequalities and Simultaneous Inequalities

key_big: Reverse the sign when you multiply or divide by a negative number.
key_sub: Simultaneous inequalities must all be true: solve each, then combine the ranges.
body_html:
How it works

  • Solve an inequality like an equation, but when you multiply or divide by a negative number, reverse the sign.
  • Simultaneous inequalities must both be true. Solve each one, then combine them, for example −2 < x ≤ 5.
  • For a double inequality such as 3 < 2x + 1 ≤ 9, do the same to all three parts.
  • On a number line, a filled circle means the end point is included (≤ or ≥); an open circle means it is not (< or >).
Example

Solve 3 < 2x + 1 ≤ 9.

Subtract 1: 2 < 2x ≤ 8

Divide by 2

Answer: 1 < x ≤ 4

Example

Find the integers that satisfy both 3x − 2 ≥ −8 and 5 − x > 1.

3x ≥ −6, so x ≥ −2

−x > −4, so x < 4 (sign reversed)

Answer: −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to reverse the sign when dividing by a negative number.
  • Dividing only the middle part of a double inequality.
  • Including an end point that has < or >.
  • Listing integers outside the range, or missing 0.

faq.a: Two or more inequalities that must all be true at the same time. Solve each one and find the values that satisfy all of them, such as −2 < x ≤ 5.

faq.q: When do I reverse the inequality sign?
faq.a: Only when you multiply or divide both sides by a negative number. Adding or subtracting never changes the sign.

faq.q: How do I find the integer solutions?
faq.a: Find the range first, then list the whole numbers inside it. Include an end point only if the sign is ≤ or ≥.

faq.q: How do I show the solution on a number line?
faq.a: Draw a line between the end points. Use a filled circle for ≤ or ≥ and an open circle for < or >.
